cluster_summary: This cluster comprises 15 CVEs in various HTML sanitizer libraries (e.g., bleach, sanitize-html, DOMPurify). The vulnerabilities arise from a range of coding mistakes: incorrect assumptions about DOM node iteration, incomplete denylists for dangerous tags and URI schemes, flawed regex patterns for attribute/value validation, missing decoding of CSS or HTML entities before security checks, and logic errors in sanitizer configuration handling. These flaws allow attackers to bypass sanitization and inject malicious scripts, resulting in cross-site scripting (XSS).
guideline_text: Trace attacker-controlled resource identifiers, namespace IDs, tenant IDs, object IDs, or bulk-operation targets carried in a request body into bulk updates, synchronization operations, mutations, or administrative effects that act on those body-selected resources. Report code paths where the body-selected resources are not validated to match the URL path parameters or the resource identity used by the authorization check. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 2 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should validate every body-selected target against the path-scoped resource identity before the permission check and before the mutation.

mechanism.missing_guard: the body-selected resources are not validated to match the URL path parameters or the resource identity used by the authorization check
mechanism.name: request-body resource identifiers bypass path-scoped authorization
mechanism.sink_shape: bulk updates, synchronization operations, mutations, or administrative effects that act on those body-selected resources
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-controlled resource identifiers, namespace IDs, tenant IDs, object IDs, or bulk-operation targets carried in a request body
mechanism.typical_fix: validate every body-selected target against the path-scoped resource identity before the permission check and before the mutation

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Use `childNodes()` to iterate all node types, iterate over all children in style elements, and capture the initial node count then iterate backwards to safely remove extraneous nodes.
sub_patterns.name: incomplete iteration over DOM child nodes during sanitization
sub_patterns.root_cause: The sanitizer assumes that only specific types or counts of child nodes exist (e.g., only element nodes, exactly one child, static NodeList length), causing it to skip dangerous content (e.g., comment nodes, extra child nodes, or nodes shifted by removal).

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Distinguish between undefined and empty explicit configuration (e.g., check `hasOwn` or `length` before falling back), and enforce the forbidden-tag check independently of the allow function.
sub_patterns.name: sanitizer configuration logic errors
sub_patterns.root_cause: The code either falls back to permissive defaults when empty allow-lists are provided (treating empty as 'not provided') or short-circuits the forbidden-tag check when a custom allow function returns true, allowing unrestricted tags.
